summary_md:
**Strongest assumption:** UK SME lenders' heads of credit and lending-ops leads are active on LinkedIn and would hire an individual engineer they watched build. Nothing in the bet or project docs shows either; the 20-target activity count hasn't been run.
**Weakest evidence:** 'Problem in their words' is marked ASSUMPTION and no buyer has said it. 'Why now' uses secondhand, platform-wide LinkedIn stats (the research doc says to trust direction only) that say nothing about this segment. Tier: opinion.
**Credibility conflict:** the planned opening post says the guard catches invented figures, but the 7 Nov panel failed v0.1 on exactly that (C1: `£48k`/`£1.2m` pass as grounded). If an outside analyst runs a statement through it before C1–C6 are fixed, the main claim is disproved.
**Pre-mortem 1:** the posts get engagement from engineers and AI builders, not lenders. The tally fills with peers, inbound calls from the segment stay at zero, and the week-3 outreach calls hide that because nobody tagged where calls came from.
**Pre-mortem 2:** it stops early. The contract check finds an outside-work or conflict clause, or 3 posts a week alongside a full-time job falls apart by week 3. The 2-week time budget doesn't cover a 6-week read window.

questions.context: Problem in their words is an ASSUMPTION. Before post 1, has any head of credit, lending-ops lead or lender CTO actually said they distrust AI underwriting because they can't trace the figures? Needs interviews (e.g. 5 people from the NACFB list), not memory.
options: Yes: 3 or more conversations, with their wording written down
1–2 informal mentions (anecdote)
No: it comes from the research doc and the playbook
Don't know

questions.context: Is the segment on LinkedIn at all? Evidence task 1 (how many of the 20 outreach targets posted or commented in the last 30 days) hasn't been run. If 3 or fewer, the channel is wrong whatever the algorithm does.
options: 10 or more of 20 are active
4–9 of 20 are active
3 or fewer of 20 are active
Don't know: not pulled yet

questions.context: The 'baseline zero' leaves out the starting audience. The 'interest graph' still needs some first readers in the segment. Export your LinkedIn connections and count those whose title or company matches the 'who' (credit, lending ops, CTO at UK SME lenders or brokers).
options: 50 or more in the segment
10–49 in the segment
Fewer than 10 in the segment
Don't know: not exported yet

questions.context: Attribution and readability: the playbook's week-3 outreach to 10 brokers and lenders falls inside the same 6 weeks, so outreach calls will be counted as post-driven. 'Target segment' has no named list, and LinkedIn's free tier doesn't show reliable job titles for profile viewers. How will the tally separate the two?
options: Tag every DM and call by source (post / outreach / other) and count only post-sourced ones against the bet
Push the outreach back to week 7 so the window only measures posts
Fix a named list of about 40 target accounts up front and count only contacts from it
Don't know

questions.context: Credibility: the 7 Nov panel failed v0.1 (C1 blocker: invented `£48k`/`£1.2m` pass the guard; C3: sign error flips the policy). The bet asks for an outside analyst to run a statement through the agent in this window. What ships before the first post on 9 Nov?
options: C1–C6 fixed and panel run 02 passes before post 1; start date moves if needed
Post now, but lead with the panel failure as the build story and hold the 'run your statement' ask until it passes
Post as planned on the current v0.1
Don't know

questions.context: Buying path: today they hire agencies or vendors they already know, which is tolerable partly because those firms already passed vendor and outsourcing due diligence. Would a UK SME lender take on an individual freelancer outside that? Ask 3 heads of credit how they found and onboarded their last outside tech supplier.
options: Directly, through a referral or LinkedIn contact, with light onboarding
Only through an approved vendor or consultancy, so partnering or subcontracting is the real route
Only for paid advisory or assessment work, not production systems
Don't know

questions.context: Gate: evidence task 2 (contract social-media and IP clauses) is unresolved, and the bet's own kill criterion depends on it. A clause on outside work, conflict of interest or competing with the employer could stop public work on a lending product, even with no employer named.
options: Checked: posting and building the product are allowed
Checked: needs employer approval or a disclosure first
Checked: blocks it, so the plan has to change
Don't know: not checked yet

proposals.text: Keep the rating at 'opinion'. The problem statement is an unverified assumption, and the only cited data is platform-wide LinkedIn reach stats, which don't speak to this segment. Moving to 'anecdote' needs 3 or more buyer conversations with their wording written down. Moving to 'data' needs the 20-target activity count and the connections export.
Before post 1: run the 20-target LinkedIn activity count and the contract clause check (both already listed), and fix C1–C6 so the opening post's claim is true.

Make the outcome readable: fix a named target-account list now, tag every DM and call by source (post / outreach / other), and only count post-sourced contacts from the list against the kill criteria.
2026-11-07: Platform-wide LinkedIn engagement stats are evidence about the format, not that a given buyer segment is on LinkedIn. Check the segment's activity before choosing the channel.
